newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 26.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

* ANAHEIM, California - Walt Disney officials won stockholder approval for Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Eisner's new 10-year employment contract, despite some angry protests directed at Eisner's lucrative compensation plan, which critics have claimed could be worth up to $400 million. Shareholders also criticised the company's $90 million-plus compensation package to former president Michael Ovitz.

* NEW YORK - Fresh questions arose Tuesday about the financing of News Corp's alliance with EchoStar Communications legal issues facing the combined company. Contrary to reports out of Monday's presentation to analysts and reporters, EchoStar executives revealed Tuesday that News Corp's only cash commitment to EchoStar is money to finish the construction of News Corp.'s satellites being transferred to EchoStar.

* WASHINGTON - Rep. Tom Coburn criticised General Electric's NBC network on Tuesday for airing an unedited version of Academy Award winning "Schindler's List," which he said brought television "to an all-time low with full frontal nudity, violence and profanity."

* HOLLYWOOD - Out of 227 screenings scheduled to appear at the American Film Market when it opens Thursday, more than 10 percent are features that appeared at the Sundance Film Festival, and nearly two-thirds of the 66 films screened at the festival will be included or have already been acquired by AFMA companies.

* NEW YORK - "Schindler's List" and "Asteroid, Part 2" have ensured a huge NBC win as the February sweeps head into their final days. "Schindler's List" posted heroic numbers with its 210-minute, commercial-free broadcast premiere, attracting an estimated 65 million viewers, more than double the number that saw it in U.S. movie theatres.
